bowlMaterials.name: Bisphenol-A Polycarbonate (BPA-PC)
bowlMaterials.shatterFailureMode: Brittle catastrophic hoop rupture under centrifugal impulse
bowlMaterials.description: High optical transparency and initial impact toughness, but subject to rapid alkaline ester hydrolysis and thermal micro-fissuring in dishwashers.

bowlMaterials.name: Tritan Copolyester (PCTG, BPA-Free)
bowlMaterials.crazingSensitivity: Low (Chemically resistant to commercial rinse aids & alkaline tabs)
bowlMaterials.shatterFailureMode: Ductile yielding and localized crazing without fragmentation
bowlMaterials.description: Engineered copolyester providing superior hydrolytic stability. Withstands over 500 dishwasher cycles without deep structural micro-cracking.

bowlMaterials.name: Heavy-Duty Tempered Borosilicate Glass
bowlMaterials.crazingSensitivity: Zero (Chemically inert to all detergents, acids & enzymes)
bowlMaterials.shatterFailureMode: Catastrophic explosive fragmentation if struck by detached metal shard
bowlMaterials.description: Impervious to chemical crazing and scratch hazing, but possesses zero ductility. High-speed projectile impact causes immediate brittle pulverization.

bowlMaterials.name: Styrene Acrylonitrile (SAN / Budget Copolymer)
bowlMaterials.crazingSensitivity: Very High (Vulnerable to citrus oils, alcohol and hot water)
bowlMaterials.shatterFailureMode: Fast crack propagation and brittle shell breakout
bowlMaterials.description: Rigid budget polymer with minimal impact absorption. Subject to rapid environmental stress cracking and brittle puncture.

bladeMetallurgies.name: AISI 420 Martensitic Stainless Steel (Standard S-Blade)
bladeMetallurgies.microChippingRisk: High under rock-ice, date pits, or bone fragment impacts
bladeMetallurgies.corrosionResistance: Moderate (Pit corrosion in acidic vinegar/salted purees)
bladeMetallurgies.description: Standard hardened cutlery alloy. Delivers keen cutting edges but exhibits notch-sensitive micro-chipping along root radius under impact.

bladeMetallurgies.name: AISI 301/304 Austenitic Stainless Steel (Budget Stamped Blade)
bladeMetallurgies.microChippingRisk: Very Low (Plastic deformation / bending rather than spalling)
bladeMetallurgies.description: Ductile and corrosion-resistant. Dulls rapidly under tough foods and bends under severe overload, but rarely sheds brittle metal fragments.

bladeMetallurgies.name: Titanium Nitride (TiN) Coated AISI 440C High-Carbon Steel
bladeMetallurgies.microChippingRisk: Moderate (Substrate flexure can spall brittle ceramic coating)
bladeMetallurgies.description: Premium commercial grade. Razor sharp and wear-resistant, but high hardness reduces impact toughness against unexpected foreign hard objects.

bladeMetallurgies.name: Glass-Filled Nylon Spindle Hub with 420 Stainless Wings
bladeMetallurgies.microChippingRisk: Moderate (High spline creep and hub thermal softening)
bladeMetallurgies.description: Hybrid construction. The glass-reinforced nylon drive hub absorbs initial shock but softens when motor shaft temperature exceeds 75°C (167°F).

foodMatrices.name: Soft Emulsions & Cooked Purees (Hummus, Mayo, Boiled Squash)
foodMatrices.shearDescription: Uniform Newtonian/non-Newtonian fluid drag with zero impulsive kinetic shock.

foodMatrices.name: Fibrous & Root Vegetables (Raw Carrots, Beets, Celery, Ginger)
foodMatrices.shearDescription: Cyclical pulsating shear resistance, producing oscillating cantilever deflection at blade root.

foodMatrices.name: Heavy Yeast Dough / Sourdough Kneading (High Torsion)
foodMatrices.shearDescription: Continuous extreme motor torque transfer, causing elevated shear heating in the spindle hub.

foodMatrices.name: Rock-Hard Frozen Fruit, Solid Ice Cubes & Whole Spices
foodMatrices.shearDescription: Severe high-frequency impact shock spikes exceeding blade tip dynamic yield threshold.

foodMatrices.name: Foreign Object Strike (Peach Pit, Olive Stone, Bone, Teaspoon)
foodMatrices.shearDescription: Instantaneous kinetic deceleration; peak shock wave exceeds fracture toughness (K1c), triggering metal cleavage.

dishwasherAging.name: Strict Hand Wash Only (Ambient Temp, Neutral Soap, 0 Cycles)
dishwasherAging.description: Zero alkaline saponification or thermal fatigue. Polymer matrix retains 100% of manufactured tensile ductility.

dishwasherAging.name: Occasional Dishwasher Cleaning (1–25 Cycles, Eco / Top Rack)
dishwasherAging.description: Incipient polymer chain degradation; localized stress whitening near handle anchor bosses.

dishwasherAging.name: Regular Dishwasher Cycles (26–100 Cycles, Normal 55°C Wash)
dishwasherAging.description: Network of optical micro-fissures radiating from center drive hub. Tensile impact resistance reduced by nearly 40%.

dishwasherAging.name: Severe Dishwasher Aging (100+ Cycles, Heated Dry, Caustic Tablets)
dishwasherAging.description: Profound chemical embrittlement and micro-fissuring. Bowl can explode into razor-sharp shards upon moderate projectile impact.

motorSpeeds.name: Low Pulse Mode (1,200 RPM / 20 Hz)
motorSpeeds.description: Gentle slicing and coarse chopping; low centrifugal inertial strain on blade root.

motorSpeeds.name: Standard Continuous Processing (1,750 RPM / 29.2 Hz)
motorSpeeds.description: Baseline residential food processor operating speed for pureeing, emulsifying, and slicing.

motorSpeeds.name: High-Speed Turbo Chop (2,400 RPM / 40 Hz)
motorSpeeds.description: High centrifugal acceleration. Unbalanced loads generate destructive oscillating radial bearing loads.

motorSpeeds.name: Commercial Heavy-Duty Machine (3,200 RPM / 53.3 Hz)
motorSpeeds.description: Industrial cutter speed. Blade tips exceed 114 km/h (71 mph); centrifugal acceleration surpasses 1,000 times gravity.

bladeFatigueHistory.name: Brand New Blade (< 5 Operating Hours)
bladeFatigueHistory.description: Pristine factory ground bevel; smooth root radius with zero notch stress concentration.

bladeFatigueHistory.name: Moderate Service (5–40 Operating Hours)
bladeFatigueHistory.description: Minor edge dulling; micro-dents from accidental contact with spatulas or hard seeds.

bladeFatigueHistory.name: Heavily Fatigued (> 40 Operating Hours, Repeated Shock)
bladeFatigueHistory.description: Pronounced notch fatigue; micro-cracks propagating inward from the S-blade root junction.
